question: A shopkeeper marks a mobile phone for ₹15,000 but allows a discount of 10%. What amount does the customer actually pay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Marked Price (MP)** × (100 − **Discount%**) ÷ 100.

**SP** = 15,000 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100 = 15,000 × 0.90.

**SP** = 13,500.

The customer pays 13,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹15,000, **Discount Rate** = 10%.

Formulas: **Discount Amount** = (**MP** × **Discount%**) ÷ 100 | **SP** = **MP** − **Discount Amount**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7af182d5c3679fe7a9f968ac706e0180e4254695ac883b72aa6c5931b368c9fd.png] 

⇒ **Discount Amount** = (15,000 × 10) ÷ 100 = ₹1,500.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 15,000 − 1,500 = ₹13,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price listed on the product. **Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

Net Selling Price

The price at which the item is sold after reducing the discount from the **Marked Price** is the **Selling Price**.
